change.title: pr-2-flat
change.description: Optimize spans buffer insertion with eviction during insert
change.author: Cristian Sotomayor

findings.title: `member` can be None; the check now runs on every request, not just optimized ones
findings.body: `organization_context.member` is `RpcOrganizationMember | None` (src/sentry/organizations/services/organization/model.py:346). `enable_advanced` is computed before the `use_optimized` check, so every call to this endpoint now evaluates `organization_context.member.has_global_access`. For a non-superuser whose context has no `member`, that raises AttributeError and returns a 500 on the default listing, which worked before this PR. Compute it only when `use_optimized` is true, and handle `member is None`. Also remove the trailing whitespace on lines 72 and 89.

findings.title: Negative-offset branch slices the queryset with a negative start, which Django rejects
findings.body: `Cursor.from_string` accepts any int offset (src/sentry/utils/cursors.py:59), so an admin can send `?optimized_pagination=true&cursor=0:-5:0`. The new branch then runs `queryset[cursor.offset:stop]` with a negative start. Django querysets do not support negative slicing: they raise an assertion or ValueError, so the request most likely ends in an unhandled 500. I did not see anything in `paginate` that turns that into a 4xx. The comments at 874-879 say Django 'properly handles negative slicing' and that this 'enables access to data beyond normal pagination bounds'. Both claims are false, and the 'permissions are checked at the queryset level' reasoning does not make the feature work. The branch has no working use. Either drop `OptimizedCursorPaginator` and the `optimized_pagination` query param, or validate and reject negative offsets with a 400. There is also no test for the new paginator.

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator copies BasePaginator.get_result and adds nothing
findings.body: Apart from the dead negative-offset branch, `get_item_key`, `value_from_cursor` and `get_result` are line-for-line copies of `Paginator` and `BasePaginator.get_result`. The 'optimized query path' and 'streamlined boundary handling' in the docstring do not exist. It is a second copy of the pagination logic that has to be kept in sync with the base class. It is also reachable only through a user-supplied query param (`optimized_pagination`), which is an undocumented public API surface. Note the base `get_result` has a second extra blank line at 819-820 (formatter would flag).

findings.title: Shared BasePaginator now silently clamps negative offsets for non-prev cursors
findings.body: Every `BasePaginator` subclass (DateTimePaginator, Paginator and others) is affected by this change, not just the audit log endpoint. Before, `queryset[offset:stop]` with a negative offset raised. Now a crafted cursor such as `0:-3:0` is clamped to 0 and returns the first page, so a malformed cursor yields a wrong-looking result with no error. For `is_prev` the offset is still passed through unchanged, so the behaviour differs between the two directions. The comment 'allow negative offsets ... underlying queryset will handle boundary conditions' does not match the code, which clamps for non-prev and passes negative through for prev. This also changes behaviour for all paginated endpoints for no stated reason. Revert this hunk.

findings.title: Comment on Cursor.offset claims negative offsets are supported
findings.body: The added comment says negative offsets are allowed for 'efficient reverse pagination'. The code is unchanged (`int(offset)`), and negative offsets are not supported by the paginators or by Django slicing. The comment is misleading; remove it.

findings.title: ZUNIONSTORE uses the default SUM aggregate, which distorts scores for duplicate payloads
findings.body: The old SUNIONSTORE deduplicated identical payloads. ZUNIONSTORE defaults to `AGGREGATE SUM`, so when the same payload is in both keys, for example a redelivered Kafka message that was ZADDed twice and then merged, its score becomes 2×`end_timestamp_precise`. Scores are now the eviction key for `zpopmin` at line 63, so a duplicated span would be treated as 'newest' and survive, while genuine newer spans are evicted. Pass `AGGREGATE MAX` (or MIN) at lines 47 and 53. Plain ZADD at buffer.py:197 overwrites the score, so that path is fine.

findings.title: Over-limit segments are silently truncated; no metric or log, and the old guard is gone
findings.body: Before, a segment over `max_segment_spans` was dropped with a metric (`segment_span_count_exceeded`) and an error log. Now `zpopmin` silently discards the oldest spans inside Redis, and the Python-side check and metric are deleted (buffer.py:446-449). Spans are lost with no signal. The loss also happens at insert time, so it cannot be observed from flush_segments. Return the evicted count from the script and emit a metric from `process_spans`. The constructor parameter `max_segment_spans` (buffer.py:150, 158) is now unused. It defaults to 1001 while the script hardcodes 1000, so the two limits can drift apart. Pass the limit in as an ARGV instead.

findings.title: Redirect-depth loop limit lowered 10000 → 1000 with no explanation, and the comment about the limit was removed
findings.body: The loop bound is unrelated to the eviction feature in the PR title. Segment trees deeper than 1000 now stop following redirects early and are no longer joined correctly, which the removed comment used to warn about. If the reduction is deliberate, say why in the PR and keep a comment. Otherwise revert.

findings.title: Set→sorted-set type change on the same key names has no rollout path
findings.body: The keys `span-buf:s:{...}:...` keep their names but change from Redis SET to ZSET. During a deploy, or for up to `redis_ttl` (3600s) afterwards, existing set keys make ZADD/ZCARD/ZUNIONSTORE fail with WRONGTYPE. Any old consumer still running during the rollout will fail with SADD against a new zset. Because the ZADD pipeline (line 197-201) and the script run in separate pipelines, one WRONGTYPE aborts the batch and the consumer crashes or retries. Consider a new key prefix (for example `span-buf:z:`), or document the required flush or drain before deploying.

findings.title: No test covers eviction or score ordering; every span has the same timestamp
findings.body: All spans use `end_timestamp_precise=1700000000.0`, so the tests cannot detect wrong ordering, the SUM-aggregate issue, or a broken `zpopmin`. There is no test that inserts more than 1000 spans and checks that the oldest are evicted. The earlier max-span test no longer exists, and nothing replaces it. There is also no test for `OptimizedCursorPaginator` or the `optimized_pagination` param.

contracts.action: New optional `optimized_pagination=true` query param on the audit log list, gated on superuser or global access
contracts.equivalent_path: The existing `self.paginate(... paginator_cls=DateTimePaginator ...)` branch at line 85
contracts.before_after: Before: always DateTimePaginator. After: OptimizedCursorPaginator for admins who pass the param. It copies BasePaginator.get_result but uses `Paginator.get_item_key` (int(floor(value))) on a datetime field, whereas DateTimePaginator converts the datetime to a ms timestamp (paginator.py:233-241). OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key calls `math.floor(datetime)` and `value_from_cursor` returns the raw cursor value.
contracts.visible_effect: The admin path would feed a datetime to math.floor, which raises TypeError. It also compares the raw cursor value against the datetime column. The optimized path is therefore broken for `-datetime` ordering for any request with a non-empty result.
contracts.failure_mode: Unhandled 500 on `optimized_pagination=true`. `member` None also 500s the default path.

contracts.action: Spans buffer moves from SADD/SSCAN to ZADD/ZSCAN with score end_timestamp_precise, plus ZPOPMIN eviction in Lua
contracts.equivalent_path: The previous sadd / sunionstore / sscan flow and the `segment_span_count_exceeded` check in `_load_segment_data`
contracts.before_after: Before: over-sized segment skipped whole with metric + log. After: oldest spans silently popped at insert; no metric; the max_segment_spans parameter is unused.
contracts.visible_effect: Segments with more than 1000 spans are flushed truncated with no error signal. Duplicate payloads get summed scores.
contracts.failure_mode: WRONGTYPE on keys left from the old version during rollout. Missing `end_timestamp_precise` in a payload would raise KeyError in factory.py:141 and crash the batch. Downstream process_segments code treats the field as required, so I treated that as acceptable.

summary: The PR bundles two unrelated changes, and both have problems. The audit-log `optimized_pagination` path and `OptimizedCursorPaginator` look broken or pointless. Their comments say Django negative slicing works, which is false. I think `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key` calls `math.floor` on a datetime. I did not read the Django slicing code or run anything. `member` can be None, so the new check can 500 even the default audit-log listing, and a hunk in shared `BasePaginator` silently clamps negative offsets. The spans-buffer move to sorted sets silently truncates over-limit segments with no metric and uses SUM aggregation on duplicate payloads. It has no rollout plan for the old SET keys, and the redirect-depth limit was cut 10x without explanation. Tests only add the new field and never exercise eviction or the new paginator.
